decision_question: Does the localized gain conceal a regression sufficient to abandon the approach?
hypothesis: Shortening the wing creates a bulky shoulder mound with blunt overlapping plates, sacrificing the canon's thin tapered metal construction even while reducing the hanging silhouette.

evidence.observation: Broad bright lumpy shoulder tiers and blunt seams replace the baseline's longer narrow feather-like shingles.
Shoulder reads as thick clustered scales; lower wing retains tapered plates, making construction inconsistent.
Slender tapered shoulder shingles are more legible, although baseline wing hangs too far.
Compact convex shield has many thin scalloped, tapered overlapping plates, rather than stacked block-like tiers.

smallest_decisive_test: Same-camera baseline/candidate side-profile crop under supplied neutral light, checking outer compactness separately from plate edge sharpness and thickness; compare to pinned JPEG shoulder at equal displayed shoulder size.
test_result: Available side view supports a localized plate-construction regression. Matched fullbird views retain torso, legs and stance; no new whole-bird proportion collapse is apparent. Thus the stronger claim that this defect requires abandoning the entire approach does not survive available evidence.
recommendation: Continue with limits; retain crown/neck and compact envelope, but reopen shoulder plate construction before calling the integrated shoulder a source-construction gain.
limitations: No new render or geometry inspection performed
Pinning follows supplied frozen manifest; image hashes not rechecked
Not owner likeness acceptance; not release approval
